fun_facts: Jahmyr Gibbs was born in Dalton, Georgia, and his hometown high school retired his No. 1 jersey.
In his senior year at Dalton High, Jahmyr Gibbs led Georgia with 2,554 rushing yards and 40 touchdowns; he finished high school with 4,882 rushing yards and 70 touchdowns.
Jahmyr Gibbs’s first college touch was a 75-yard kickoff return.
As a Georgia Tech freshman, Jahmyr Gibbs recorded 763 yards from scrimmage and seven touchdowns.
Jahmyr Gibbs is also known by the nickname “Sonic.”

basis.reasoning: The profile lists Georgia Tech followed by Alabama under college, so Alabama is the last college listed.

excerpts:
nfl.com%2fnews-events%2fnews-and-features%2fdetroit-lions-rb-jahmyr-gibbs-has-high-school-number-retired%2f)

There will never be another Dalton Catamount high school football player wearing No. 1. That’s because the northwest Georgia school has retired the number that once belonged to current Detroit running back Jahmyr Gibbs.

Friday night, Gibbs returned to his hometown for a ceremony to retire his high school number.

“All the love and support I get back home means a lot. So, every time I come back home, it’s always fun,” said Gibbs, who ran for 945 yards in his rookie NFL season, averaging 5.2 yards per carry.

During his senior season at Dalton, Gibbs led the state with 2,554 rushing yards, scoring 40 touchdowns. He finished his scholastic career with 4,882 rushing yards and 70 touchdowns.

“Jahmyr had a great career in college, and he’s had a wonderful first year as a pro.

excerpts: In 2021, Gibbs was coming off a brilliant freshman season at Georgia Tech, which he began by returning a kickoff 75 yards on his first college touch and wrapped up with 763 yards from scrimmage and seven TDs. Choice, the Yellow Jackets' running backs coach at the time, anointed Gibbs as a team leader and wanted him to address the rest of the squad.
